Previosly we were using the class method for fetching the column names
and not considering the local query based aliasing in column names.
Using the instance level method covers up for it.

issue_context.title: Do not show user_name when I use AS
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

``` ruby
require 'bundler/inline'

gemfile(true) do
  source 'https://rubygems.org'

  git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

  gem 'activerecord'
  gem 'sqlite3'
end

require 'active_record'
require 'minitest/autorun'
require 'logger'

ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: 'sqlite3', database: ':memory:')
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :users, force: true do |t|
    t.string :name
  end
end

class User < ActiveRecord::Base; end

class TemplateTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_inspect
    User.create!(name: :alice)

    assert_equal "#<ActiveRecord::Relation [#<User id: nil, user_name: \"alice\">]>", User.select('name AS user_name').inspect
  end
end
```
### Expected behavior

```ruby
"#<ActiveRecord::Relation [#<User id: nil, user_name: \"alice\">]>"
```

### Actual behavior

```ruby
"#<ActiveRecord::Relation [#<User id: nil>]>"
```

### System configuration

**Rails version**:master

**Ruby version**:2.7.0


### Reference

- https://github.com/pry/pry/issues/2083#issuecomment-548386171
- https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/8ab9daf2803
comments: Hey, I would like to work on this issue, as it seems a good learning opportunity.
I think you meant to say, show `user_name` when you use `AS` @taki

> I think you meant to say, show user_name when you use AS @taki

yes.

@taki @yashLadha I hacked around a bit and found that using `self.attribute_names` instead of `self.class.attribute_names` does solve the issue.
Related diff:
```ruby
diff --git a/activerecord/lib/active_record/core.rb b/activerecord/lib/active_record/core.rb
index f879abdd28..0525556844 100644
--- a/activerecord/lib/active_record/core.rb
+++ b/activerecord/lib/active_record/core.rb
@@ -523,7 +523,7 @@ def inspect
       # We check defined?(@attributes) not to issue warnings if the object is
       # allocated but not initialized.
       inspection = if defined?(@attributes) && @attributes
-        self.class.attribute_names.collect do |name|
+        self.attribute_names.collect do |name|
           if has_attribute?(name)
             attr = _read_attribute(name)
             value = if attr.nil?

```
A little change is needed in the assertion of the test case provided, `id` comes later than user defined attribute as it is default attribute.
```ruby
-    assert_equal "#<ActiveRecord::Relation [#<User id: nil, user_name: \"alice\">]>", User.select('name AS user_name').inspect
+    assert_equal "#<ActiveRecord::Relation [#<User user_name: \"alice\", id: nil>]>", User.select('name AS user_name').inspect
```

I am not familiar with `ActiveRecord` 's codebase so not sure if this is the right solution.
This is because it is calling the active model instance level method and not the class method. The instance-level method uses the query level column names also for initialization.
